Urogynecology in Worli

It is a specialized branch of gynecology which deals with women suffering from the pelvic floor disorders. Most of the urogynaecology issues are experienced by the women in the menopausal and peri menopausal age, however it is not uncommon to see these disorders in the younger women. The disorders which are dealt with here are urinary incontinence or leakages, pelvic organ prolapses and overactive bladders.

Pelvic organ prolapses are when the pelvic organs of the women that is the uterus, bladder rectum have dropped down from their original positions and the women generally complain of something coming out through their vagina. There are various treatment modalities which are available depending on the women’s age group from hysterectomy that is removal of the uterus through the vagina or sling surgeries that is pulling the uterus up and anchoring it to its surrounding structures.

Many a times damage to the pelvic floor and damage to the nerve supply to the adjacent areas can cause leaking of urine on straining. Though most of the women are embarrassed talking about this situation it is important to make them aware of it as it decreases their quality of life. There are various treatment modalities available right from lifestyle changes to certain minimally invasive surgeries like bladder slings and insertion of no tapes and meshes for the bladder neck supports.

Yes — as of May 2026, there has been an international move to rename Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) to Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS).

The change was proposed because the old name “PCOS” was considered misleading:

Many people with the condition do not actually have ovarian cysts.
The condition affects the whole endocrine and metabolic system, not just the ovaries.
It is linked with insulin resistance, weight changes, fertility issues, androgen excess, cardiovascular risk, and mental health effects.

“PMOS” stands for:

Polyendocrine → multiple hormone systems involved
Metabolic → insulin and metabolism effects
Ovarian → ovarian/reproductive involvement
Syndrome → group of related symptoms

featured_reviews.name: ruchi pujara
featured_reviews.review_text:
Where do I even start?

I went to Dr. Ojha for a second opinion because the previous doctor I was seeing simply wasn’t really listening to me. There was very little effort to help me understand why things were happening to my body. Instead, I often left feeling like everything was somehow my fault, which created a lot of anxiety and self-doubt. It felt more like judgment than a real attempt to understand what the patient was going through.

While I was getting my ultrasound done, I happened to speak with Dr. Vaidya about my situation, and she recommended Dr. Ojha for a second opinion. I managed to get an appointment with Dr. Ojha the very next day.

From the moment I walked in, the experience was completely different. Dr. Ojha went through my entire case file—from 2023 until now—very carefully. She actually listened to me. I had a whole list of questions, and she patiently heard me out for nearly 20 minutes. Then she spent a good amount of time explaining everything in detail.

What really stood out to me was that she had already gone through my reports and asked me about my symptoms and pain even before I mentioned them.

She prescribed medication, which I’ve now been on for 17 days, and the difference is already incredible. For the past 2.5 years I hadn’t felt like myself. Within just a few weeks, the mental fog started lifting. The anxiety and heaviness I had been carrying slowly began to ease. I didn’t even realize how unwell I had been feeling until I started feeling like my old self again.

So yes, I would recommend her 100%.

I genuinely cannot thank her enough. Before meeting her, trying to deal with my PCOD had reached a point where I honestly felt like I was going crazy.

Thank you for helping me find my way back to myself, Dr. Ojha.
